items.s: The two reports measure different things, so they do not ____ each other.
It is hard to ____ on homework when your phone keeps making noise.

A study ____ in 2025 looked at how Americans spent their time.

tfn.s: Naomi Alderman's plan lasted eight weeks.
tfn.why: The text says: "In August 2026, the novelist Naomi Alderman described an eight-week plan to help people get back into reading."

tfn.s: A 2025 study looked at how Americans spent their time from 2003 to 2023.
tfn.why: The text says: "A study published in 2025 looked at how Americans spent their time between 2003 and 2023."

tfn.s: Naomi Alderman's plan aimed to help people finish as many books as possible.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "The aim was not to finish as many books as possible, but to enjoy the habit again."

tfn.s: The plan has been tried by thousands of readers.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say how many people have tried the plan.

tfn.s: The text says phones are the only reason people read less.
tfn.why: The text says phones "may be part of the problem" and that people also need time, quiet places and interesting books.

focus.note: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word. The small word changes the meaning, so learn them together.

items.s: Someone might begin with ten minutes and then work ____ longer reading sessions.
Switch your phone ____ for a while if you want to read.
The writer described a plan to help people get ____ into reading.
A book asks us to stay ____ one story for longer.
Keep your phone out of reach so you do not pick it ____ every minute.
She has the physical ____ to run for an hour without needing a rest.
The police said they had found no ____ that anyone had broken in.
Work, money and family are common ____ that leave people too tired to read.
Her ____ as a pianist was obvious when she was six, and teachers soon noticed it.
He felt a strong ____ to leave his job and travel the world.
The latest ____ are surprising: they show a rise in some groups and a fall in others.

match.d: giving all your attention to one thing
the first thing people blame for a problem
small enough to deal with easily
begin to control or fill something

items.s: By the time she opened the novel again, she ____ who was speaking.
When I was a child, a story ____ to me every night.
Reading habits ____ a lot in recent years.
If I switched my phone off, I ____ much more.
While I ____ my messages, the story slipped from my mind.

tfn.s: The 2025 study and the Pew survey measure the same thing.
tfn.why: The study counts reading on an average day; Pew counts adults who read at least part of a book in a year.

tfn.s: The writer thinks technology is not the only reason people read less.
tfn.why: The text says it "would be too simple to blame every change on technology".

tfn.s: Alderman's programme gives people a fixed list of books to read.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text only says the programme builds reading time gradually.

tfn.s: Reading at least part of a book in a year is more common than reading on a typical day.
tfn.why: About three-quarters read part of a book in a year, but only about 16% read on an average day.

tfn.s: The writer says everyone should spend hours reading novels.
tfn.why: The text says "The real concern is not that everyone should spend hours reading novels."

continuing for a long time without stopping
given an idea by something else
slowly, a little at a time
find something very hard to do
a famous book that people still read
the way a person lives every day
a way of doing something

focus.note: Many phrasal verbs have a meaning you cannot guess from the parts. Check what the whole phrase means in the sentence.

items.s: Be patient: after a few pages, the story will take ____ and you will stop checking the time.
Many adults have fallen ____ of the habit of reading since they left school.
When you want to focus, put your phone ____ in a drawer.
I forced myself ____ the first fifty pages, and then the book became exciting.
Sign ____ for a library card, and borrowing books costs nothing.
Constant interruptions can ____ a reader's confidence long before the last chapter.
Few readers can ____ a book that makes no effort to hold their interest.
Even keen readers find it hard to ____ the pull of a glowing screen.
Even as screens multiply, the habit of reading aloud to children continues to ____ in many families.
Critics are wrong in ____ the decline in reading entirely to one cause.
Teachers who insist on ____ comic books as lightweight may put off reluctant readers.

match.d: use a source of information or experience
keep time or money for one purpose
insecure and likely to go wrong
something shown off to appear cultured

items.s: Treating reading as a test of cultural ____ makes it less inviting.
Few readers found the critic's claim ____, since it ignored the survey data.
Critics accused the film of ____ a harsh period of history.
The ____ offered by a phone is far more immediate than that of a novel.
Someone who skips a chapter is not ____ lazy.

tfn.s: Someone who read a few pages of one book last year could count in Pew's figure without being counted in the daily-reading figure.
tfn.why: Pew counts adults who read "at least some of a book" in a year; the study counts reading on an average day.

tfn.s: The writer regards audiobooks as a poorer way to read than print.
tfn.why: The text warns against "dismissing audiobooks and digital formats as inferior".

tfn.s: Alderman's programme asks participants to keep a reading diary.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text only mentions progressively longer sessions.

tfn.s: The writer implies that difficulty concentrating does not necessarily show a personal failing.
tfn.why: The text says someone who struggles is "not necessarily lazy or incapable".

tfn.s: The writer argues that smartphones are the only pressure on reading.
tfn.why: The text says blaming digital technology for everything "glosses over other pressures".

focus.note: At this level, many phrasal verbs are idiomatic and fairly formal. Notice that the particle stays in the sentence and you supply the verb.

items.s: Politicians often ____ over the awkward details of their plans.
Doctors could not ____ out stress as a cause of the headaches.
Many adults ____ away from long novels because they fear losing the thread.
He tends to ____ aside any criticism of his habits.
Publishers may ____ down how few people finish what they buy.

speak.title: Role-play: ten minutes a day
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.role: the friend who wants to read more
a.text: You've bought lots of books but you hardly open them. Ask your friend to join you for ten quiet minutes of reading every evening, with phones off. Explain why it would help.

b.text: You're tired after work and scrolling relaxes you. Ask questions and explain your worries. You can say yes, no, or yes with a different plan.

phrases: I'd love to get back into reading.
Could we try ten minutes a day?
I'm too tired by the evening.
What if we switched our phones off?
That's a fair point, but I'd rather start small.
Let's give it a week and see how it goes.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you agree a plan, and is it realistic?
